title: Conjectures for the ECS 2.0 unit-dependence run, written before it

claims.statement: Removing a unit unrelated to the claim (neither its own argument nor a definition that argument uses) never moves the model's answer to whether the claim follows.
claims.note: A refutation says the answer moved with a unit the document's own argument does not use; whether that is the model, the position of the unit, or a dependence the pattern heuristic missed is what the loci keep open.

claims.statement: Removing a unit that defines a term the claim's own argument uses never leaves both form fields unmoved.
claims.note: A refutation says a definition the document's argument rests on did no observable work for this model; the JSON guard keeps a reply that did not parse from counting.

claims.statement: Removing the section the claim is drawn from never moves the model's answer to whether the claim follows.
claims.note: The claim is restated in the preamble; a refutation says the model needed the document's derivation and not only its definitions.

claims.statement: A byte-identical repeat of the request never moves the model's answer to whether the claim follows.
claims.note: The floor: any UDP-01 or UDP-03 refutation is read against this count.

claims.statement: On the full document a model never says that a point the document itself states does not follow.
claims.note: Every probe is a section carrying the document's own argument markup; the document says each follows.

claims.statement: On the full document a model never returns an empty list of essential terms.
claims.note: Each probed argument names at least one commitment or defined term.

claims.statement: Within a 600-second budget a call on the whole document never fails by the client's own timeout.
claims.note: Stated on the transport kind, not on every failure of delivery (H33): a 503 or a closed connection is a failure of delivery and not a timeout.
